topic: CodeGraph vs Graphify for AI Coding Agents 2026
summary: CodeGraph and Graphify both try to stop AI coding agents from repeatedly grepping and reading a repository from scratch, but they are not interchangeable. CodeGraph is narrower and deeper: a local MCP code-intelligence layer focused on symbols, call edges, dependency paths, blast radius, auto-sync, and agent queries against source code. Graphify is broader and more portable: a Python skill that turns code, docs, schemas, PDFs, images, video, and other project artifacts into graphify-out artifacts that many coding assistants can query, diff, commit, or serve. The comparison should frame CodeGraph as the stronger fit for agent-native code navigation and impact analysis, while Graphify is the stronger fit for multimodal, team-shareable project memory.

competitors.title: colbymchenry/codegraph: Pre-indexed code knowledge graph
key_points: Primary CodeGraph source. Positions CodeGraph as a local-first pre-indexed code knowledge graph for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, Gemini, Antigravity, and Kiro.
Install flow is CLI install, `codegraph install` to wire agents, then `codegraph init` per project to create the local `.codegraph/` index.
The README emphasizes MCP integration, auto-sync on file changes, local execution, symbol/call/dependency context, dynamic-dispatch-aware paths, and blast-radius analysis.

Benchmark section claims median wins across seven open-source repos: 58% fewer tool calls, 22% faster answers, and file reads cut near zero, with token/cost savings described as scale-dependent rather than universal.

competitors.title: safishamsi/graphify: AI coding assistant skill
key_points: Primary Graphify source. Describes Graphify as an AI coding assistant skill that maps code, SQL schemas, R scripts, shell scripts, docs, papers, images, and videos into a queryable knowledge graph.
Core workflow is `uv tool install graphifyy`, `graphify install`, then `/graphify .` or `$graphify` in Codex.
Graphify creates `graphify-out/graph.html`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and `graph.json`, making it more artifact-oriented than CodeGraph's hidden local project index.

README highlights broad platform support across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, VS Code Copilot Chat, Aider, Amp, OpenClaw, Factory Droid, Trae, Hermes, Kimi Code, Kiro, Pi, Devin CLI, and Google Antigravity.

Graphify supports many optional extras: MCP server, Neo4j, FalkorDB, PDF, Office, Google Workspace, video, SQL, PostgreSQL, Terraform, Ollama, OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Bedrock, and Azure-compatible backends.

competitors.title: Graphify Ships v0.8.41: A Knowledge Graph Skill for 20+ AI Coding Assistants
key_points: Strong third-party Graphify competitor article. Frames Graphify as a persistent, queryable structure layered on top of Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other assistants rather than a replacement for them.

Highlights Graphify's differentiators: local tree-sitter extraction for code, confidence tags (`EXTRACTED`, `INFERRED`, `AMBIGUOUS`), multi-source graphs, MCP server option, and git-friendly team workflow.
Important article gap: it compares Graphify mostly against built-in assistant search, not against CodeGraph, so a direct CodeGraph-vs-Graphify article can own the decision matrix.
Useful positioning line: Graphify's shared, version-controlled `graph.json` is a different workflow from each assistant rebuilding context inside its own session.

competitors.title: Local Code Graphs Are the Agent Context Layer

Useful adoption framing: start with one large repo and one workflow such as routing changes, SDK API changes, refactors, test-target selection, onboarding, or impact analysis.

Useful measurement ideas for this comparison: tool calls before first edit, file reads before first edit, wrong-file edits, missed-impact review comments, staleness incidents, and verification quality.

Good source for reader pain language, but it is light on head-to-head comparison, team governance, and when Graphify's broader artifact graph is a better fit.

The likely objection to address: tree-sitter/code graph tools can overpromise if the agent still needs source-level validation, tests, runtime behavior, and product context.
Article should acknowledge that both tools are context accelerators, not correctness engines.

stats.fact: As of July 3, 2026, `colbymchenry/codegraph` had 57,263 GitHub stars, 3,525 forks, 270 open issues, TypeScript as the primary language, and an MIT license.
As of July 3, 2026, `safishamsi/graphify` had 76,613 GitHub stars, 7,599 forks, 409 open issues, Python as the primary language, and an MIT license.
CodeGraph's repository was created on January 18, 2026 and was pushed on July 3, 2026, showing active development at research time.
Graphify's repository was created on April 3, 2026 and was pushed on July 3, 2026, showing active development at research time despite being younger than CodeGraph.
The latest npm package for `@colbymchenry/codegraph` was version 1.2.0 at research time, with optional platform packages for macOS, Linux, and Windows on x64 and arm64.
The official Graphify PyPI package is `graphifyy` with CLI command `graphify`; version 0.9.5 was uploaded on July 2, 2026 and requires Python 3.10 or newer.
CodeGraph's README says it auto-configures Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, Hermes Agent, Gemini CLI, Antigravity IDE, and Kiro.

Graphify's README lists support for more than 20 coding assistants, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, VS Code Copilot Chat, Aider, Amp, OpenClaw, Factory Droid, Trae, Hermes, Kimi Code, Kiro, Pi, Devin CLI, and Google Antigravity.
Graphify produces `graph.html`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and `graph.json` in `graphify-out/`, while CodeGraph stores its project index under `.codegraph/` after `codegraph init`.
CodeGraph's README reports benchmark results across seven open-source repos with 58% fewer tool calls, 22% faster answers, and near-zero file reads for the CodeGraph arm.
The Augment article says Graphify v0.8.41 had 68.9K GitHub stars, 136 releases, and 98 contributors at publication time, and framed it as one of the more active AI coding skill projects.
The Augment article says Graphify code extraction runs offline via tree-sitter, but docs, PDFs, images, and videos use the configured model API unless routed through local or enterprise backends.

Firecrawl's July 3, 2026 search result summary for Emelia's Graphify guide reported claimed token reduction up to 71.5x compared with traditional file reading, plus 20 programming languages and 10 IDE integrations.

angles: Lead with the decision: choose CodeGraph when the bottleneck is AI agents wasting tool calls on source-code discovery; choose Graphify when the bottleneck is missing project memory across code, docs, schemas, and diagrams.
Make the article a buyer-style comparison, not a generic knowledge graph explainer. Readers searching `CodeGraph vs Graphify` already know both names and need a workflow decision.

Use a concrete scenario table: single developer in Claude Code, Cursor team on a monorepo, onboarding to a polyglot repo, compliance-sensitive codebase, database-backed app, docs-heavy research project, and team-shared architecture map.
Address the hype gap: both tools reduce context discovery work, but neither replaces tests, runtime tracing, code review, or source validation before merging.
Explain the artifact difference clearly: CodeGraph is an agent context service; Graphify is also a shareable project artifact/report workflow.
Contrast freshness: CodeGraph's auto-sync is compelling during active edits; Graphify's git-friendly output is compelling for shared team memory but needs process discipline.
Separate local code extraction from non-code extraction. Graphify's multimodal support is valuable, but readers should understand which data paths may involve model APIs.
Use dated GitHub and package stats in a small 'maturity snapshot' box, with a warning that stars are a popularity signal, not proof of reliability.

Add an evaluation checklist: run the same task with no graph, CodeGraph, and Graphify; measure first useful answer time, tool calls, file reads, missed call sites, wrong-file edits, stale references, and review comments.

Include an objections section inspired by Reddit/direct discussion: graph tools can solve the wrong problem if the agent's real failure is unclear requirements, missing tests, runtime state, or poor verification.

recommended_verdict: For most coding-agent workflows centered on source-code edits, CodeGraph is the cleaner first pick because it is narrower, MCP-first, auto-syncs during edits, and publishes direct tool-call/file-read benchmark claims. For teams that want a visible, shareable project memory layer spanning code, docs, schemas, diagrams, PDFs, and media, Graphify is the more flexible tool. The strongest article position is not that one universally beats the other, but that CodeGraph is the agent context accelerator while Graphify is the project knowledge graph artifact.
